messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — onboarding HF model 'open-reply-2b' hit two issues when running redwood-convert: tokenizer special-token mismatch and a custom config class that needs trust_remote_code.

leo: Logs? paste the error.

maria: Here are the key bits:
```
$ redwood-convert --input hf/open-reply-2b --output rw/open-reply-2b
Loading config...
UserWarning: 'architectures' missing, falling back to generic class
AttributeError: 'CustomConfig' object has no attribute 'vocab_size'
```

angela: That smells like trust_remote_code. Did you try loading with `trust_remote_code=True`? :thinking:  

maria: Yep. `AutoConfig.from_pretrained(path, trust_remote_code=True)` lets it load, but conversion still fails later because the model's `chat_template` uses custom placeholders like `<|sep|>` that aren't in the tokenizer.

sam: Does tokenizer have an `added_special_tokens.json` or `special_tokens_map.json` in the repo? HF sometimes keeps those separate.

maria: There is `tokenizer.json` + `special_tokens_map.json`. The model expects `<|user|>` but the tokenizer has `<usr>`. So prompts get tokenized incorrectly and the chat formatter breaks.

leo: Quick patch: add a small mapping shim during conversion, e.g. `{"<|user|>": "<usr>", "<|assistant|>": "<sys>"}` and call `tokenizer.add_tokens([...])` before export. That should preserve token ids. :wrench:

maria: I tried that and proceeded to run quantization experiments (bnb 4-bit) — saw a quality regression on webqa-sample: accuracy 82.4% -> 77.6%, and PPL from 13.1 -> 16.8. Not great.

angela: 4.8% absolute hit is significant. Do we know which modules are failing under 4-bit? Custom layers often break.

maria: Model uses `CustomLMHead` subclass of `PreTrainedModel` and overrides tied embeddings. bitsandbytes throws warnings about unsupported ops in that head during quantization.

sam: Workaround: mark problematic modules as fp16 in qconfig: `{"CustomLMHead": "fp16"}` so bnb skips quantizing them. Does that help accuracy?

maria: Partially. With `CustomLMHead` in fp16 the accuracy recovers to 80.9% (still -1.5% vs float32) and latency increases ~12ms per request. CI evals also flagged chat-format mismatches: our chat formatter expects `\n\nAssistant:` boundaries but model emits ML-style tags which our postprocesser doesn't catch.

leo: Long-term plan: 1) upstream patch to expose stable config fields (so we don't need trust_remote_code), 2) conversion shim that normalizes `chat_template` -> canonical tokens (assistant/user), and 3) qconfig heuristics to fall back to fp16 for custom modules.

maria: I'm adding unit tests: tokenization round-trip, a small prompt suite, and the eval harness. I'll also open a security ticket for trust_remote_code review so we can approve this model if needed.

onboard-bot: Reminder: link the security ticket to the onboarding checklist and add the model to the manual-review queue.

sam: Can someone run `redwood-bench compare` on `rw/open-reply-2b` v1 (raw convert) vs v2 (shim + fp16 head) and upload latency/accuracy plots to the PR? :eyes:

maria: On it — pushing a conversion branch now and adding the tests. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/models/pulls/312

leo: Thanks. If conversion succeeds we should also add a small doc snippet in `docs/model-onboarding` describing the token-shim pattern so next time it's faster.

maria: Good call. I'll add that to the PR checklist.
